Why was the motor car central to the boom?
back: Mass production made cars cheap, and they boosted steel, rubber, glass, oil, roads and suburbs.

front: Why did farmers not share in the boom?
back: Overproduction, falling European demand, foreign tariffs and wartime debts drove prices and incomes down.

front: Which older industries declined in the 1920s?
back: Coal (new fuels), textiles (new fibres, competition) and railways (cars and lorries).

front: Name three weaknesses of the economy by 1929.
back: Overproduction, unequal wealth, foreign tariffs, debt and weak banks (any three).
